audit_findings.title: The $5.7 billion opioid liability may be an omitted senior cash claim
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed June 30 liability $5.660bn; 10.4% of $54.303bn base equity value, 109.6% of bridge cash, and $48.22 per diluted share before discounting
audit_findings.mechanism: Future settlement cash payments must either reduce forecast OE or be recognized as a senior claim in the equity bridge, without double counting.
audit_findings.evidence: At March 31, 2026, our estimated accrued liability for opioid-related claims was $5.7 billion.
audit_findings.explanation: The unpaid liability and scheduled payments are demonstrated, but omission is an error only if historical charges were removed from OE or forecast OE does not capture the payments. The exposure is large enough to materially reduce intrinsic value even though it would reinforce, rather than reverse, the current conclusion that $907.99 exceeds all scenario values.
audit_findings.action: Trace opioid charges, OE exclusions, accrual movements, and payments by year; rerun with scheduled payments in OE or their present value deducted from the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Apollo's convertible preferred equity may be counted as common shareholders' cash
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed $1.238bn net proceeds plus $293m Apollo redemption-value adjustment, totaling at least $1.531bn before allocated earnings; $13.04 per diluted share and 2.8% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds cash funded by Apollo while forecast OE retains consolidated Medical-Surgical economics and no preferred or redeemable minority claim is deducted.
audit_findings.evidence: As a part of the separation strategy, on April 20, 2026, the Company announced it had entered into a definitive agreement under which funds managed by affiliates of Apollo Global Management, Inc. (“Apollo Funds”) will acquire approximately 13 % minority ownership interest in the Medical‑Surgical Solutions segment through an investment of approximately $ 1.25 billion in the segment’s convertible preferred equity.
audit_findings.explanation: The preferred investment, cash proceeds, and redeemable NCI recognition are demonstrated. The precise common-equity adjustment depends on the preferred terms and allocation of Medical-Surgical OE, but recognizing the proceeds without Apollo's economic claim materially overstates value.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the preferred terms, reconcile the proceeds to June cash, allocate post-closing Medical-Surgical OE to MCK common, and model the liquidation, distribution, conversion, and redemption rights.

audit_findings.title: Post-year borrowing may have entered cash without entering owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed $3.215bn of June-quarter long-term-debt proceeds and $3.239bn of Medical-Surgical term loans; computed annual interest about $181m pre-tax or $143m after the 21.1% quarter tax rate, equal to 4.1% of anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: June cash reflects post-anchor financing while the March 2026 OE anchor lacks the corresponding recurring interest expense retained in an equity-level OE calculation.
audit_findings.evidence: The net proceeds from the Term Loan A Facilities were used by MMS Borrower for a payment of principal on an intercompany loan with the Company.
audit_findings.explanation: The timing mismatch is demonstrated, although the amount of proceeds remaining in cash is not separately identifiable. The full-run interest burden is large enough to materially lower forecast OE; retaining transaction-funded cash without that burden overstates value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $3.215bn proceeds through intercompany repayment, cash, repurchases, and other uses, then rerun OE with the full pro forma interest burden for all Medical-Surgical term loans.

audit_findings.title: Redeemable NCI and consolidated add-backs may not describe the parent-common claim
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed redeemable NCI was $943m at March 31, including $700m initial Core Ventures and $25m initial PRISM interests; Core added an $81m June-quarter redemption adjustment; consolidated add-back misallocation is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Consolidated D&A, capex, and other cash-flow adjustments can import minority economics into parent OE, while redeemable interests and put rights represent claims ahead of MCK common.
audit_findings.evidence: The 30 % minority interest is classified as redeemable noncontrolling interest, with a put option exercisable every five years .
audit_findings.explanation: The redeemable interests and Core put are demonstrated. Whether each OE add-back is misallocated remains unresolved, and redemption adjustments already reduce income attributable to MCK, creating possible offsetting conservatism. Nevertheless, the $943m opening claim alone equals $8.03 per diluted share and 1.7% of base equity value, before any add-back correction.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild every OE year using parent-attributable D&A, capex, and adjustments; reconcile redemption-value charges already included in net income; separately model PRISM and Core put payments without double counting.

audit_findings.title: The entire cash balance is treated as distributable despite working-capital dependence
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed bridge cash $5.164bn; $43.99 per diluted share and 9.5% of base equity value; unavailable operating portion unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Only cash exceeding normalized operating, seasonal, settlement, transaction, and minority-entity requirements belongs in the equity bridge as a distributable asset.
audit_findings.evidence: Our businesses require substantial investments in working capital that are susceptible to large variations during the year as a result of inventory purchase patterns and seasonal demands.
audit_findings.explanation: Adding all cash is demonstrated, while the filing demonstrates substantial working-capital variability and $220m of first-quarter operating cash use. The record does not prove how much cash is trapped or required, but the amount exposed is sufficiently large to be reasonably capable of materially changing intrinsic value.
audit_findings.action: Calculate normalized minimum cash from monthly or intra-quarter working-capital cycles, isolate transaction proceeds and minority-owned cash, and rerun the bridge using demonstrably excess cash only.

audit_findings.title: The anchor trend omits an audited intervening year
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed FY2025 parent net income $3.295bn, but FY2025 OE is unquantified; computed base sensitivity is approximately $1.405bn of equity value or $11.97 per share for each $100m change in anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: FY2025 OE enters the chronological log trend that determines the selected anchor and therefore scales projected OE, operating PV, and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Net income attributable to McKesson Corporation was $4.8 billion and $3.3 billion for the years ended March 31, 2026 and 2025, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The omission is a demonstrated methodological error because an available intervening year was excluded and the model selected trend rather than latest OE. Direction cannot be known until FY2025 OE is constructed, but the model's anchor sensitivity makes a material valuation effect reasonably possible.
audit_findings.action: Construct FY2025 OE under identical rules, audit its NCI and exceptional-item treatment, recompute the complete-series log trend, and rerun all scenarios if the selected anchor changes.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed/computed residuals: FY2017 $121m, FY2018 $145m, FY2019 $147m, and FY2024 $31m; respectively 5.0%, 6.8%, 6.9%, and 1.1% of those years' OE; valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any residual D&A proven to be an eligible non-economic expense would be added back to historical OE and could increase the trend anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2017 $121.0m (13.3% of filed D&A); FY2018 $145.0m (15.2% of filed D&A); FY2019 $147.0m (15.5% of filed D&A); FY2024 $31.0m (4.9% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: No overstatement risk is shown because the unidentified amounts remain expensed. The possible understatement is unresolved: the record neither establishes that the residual is eligible nor provides comparable amounts for all years, including FY2026, so valuation materiality cannot be determined.
audit_findings.action: Classify each residual D&A component from filed schedules or asset records, add back only amounts meeting the OE rules, and recompute the trend anchor if eligible amounts are identified.
